subject: Redlines: Order Form — staged commit, invoicing cadence & tax evidence
messages:
From: Samantha Hart <samantha.hart@harbor-analytics.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@harbor-analytics.com
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form redlines + tax certificate attached

Hi Kimberly / Ben —

Thanks for sending the latest Order Form (v3). Procurement reviewed and attached a PDF with our proposed redlines. There are three commercial items we need clearer language on before we can route to finance:

- Staged commit schedule: Harbor prefers a three-tranche commit tied to product milestones rather than a single annual prepay. We marked specific dates in the redlines (50% on signing, 30% after integration, 20% on GA).
- Invoicing cadence & PO requirements: We need net45 and a single consolidated invoice per tranche (not per deployment). Our ERP does not accept monthly token-level invoices.
- Tax evidence: Attached a PDF certificate for Harbor's tax-exempt status in the state of WA; please confirm how you intend to reflect tax liability on the invoice.

Also flagged a couple of small things: acceptance of the currency clause (USD) and need to confirm whether Redwood will issue a single annual invoice if we elect prepay.

Can you confirm whether Legal is comfortable with staged commits (and how that impacts minimum-commit proration)? If we can get a markup back by Monday we can keep our renewal committee on schedule.

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Hart
Director, Procurement
Harbor Analytics
(samantha.hart@harbor-analytics.com)

Attachments: OrderForm_Harbor_v3_redlines.pdf (pdf, 189KB); Harbor_Tax_Certificate.pdf (pdf, 120KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Order Form redlines + tax certificate attached

Thanks Samantha — received and noted (and thanks for the PDF). Looping in Aditya (sales leadership) and Neha (commercial ops/legal intake) so we can align quickly. High-level responses below; I'll bake language suggestions into a revised Order Form and share a tracked PDF.

- Staged commit: We can support staged commits but need clarity on how the minimum commitment and overage reconciliation will be handled if customer ramps. Proposed approach: treat each tranche as a separate committed period with its own usage reconciliation window; any unused committed units in a tranche do not roll forward (unless explicitly agreed). Will propose a stair-step schedule in the Order Form with explicit start/end dates per tranche.
- Invoicing cadence: Redwood typically invoices per billing period tied to committed tranche and reports tokens monthly. For ERP compatibility we can issue consolidated tranche invoices (net45) but need procurement PO number per tranche to trigger invoice generation.
- Tax evidence: We will accept the tax certificate and pass to Tax Ops for review. If Harbor is tax-exempt for WA, we'll zero-rate tax for the WA jurisdiction but may still need to collect evidence on file.

Action items:
1) Aditya / Ben: do you want Legal to accept staged-commit language or do we suggest an alternate (e.g., single commitment with staged payments)?
2) Neha: please intake the redlines and prepare a tracked Order Form to return to Samantha by EOD Monday (PST).

Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, RW Inference

Team —

I reviewed Harbor's redlines and drafted language that preserves Redwood's commercial guardrails while accommodating the staged payment preference. Summary of proposed edits (I'll attach a tracked PDF in the HubSpot record):

1) Commit structure: convert the "minimum annual commitment" into three discrete committed periods with dates and committed units per period. Each period will reconcile usage against its own committed units. If Harbor underutilizes a tranche, credits will be applied only against that tranche per the reconciliation clause; credits do not carry forward. (This protects Redwood from cross-period revenue leakage.)

2) Overages & pricing schedule: keep the per-unit overage rate consistent across tranches. Add a table row for "early ramp" pricing — if total usage before tranche end exceeds 120% of tranche commitment, apply an early-ramp credit model (reduces overage by 10% for that tranche).

3) Invoicing & POing: confirm that procurement will provide a PO per tranche. Drafted invoice language to allow a consolidated invoice per tranche with net45 payment terms; include a single invoice reference that lists included monthly token summaries as an appendix.

4) Taxes: accept Harbor's tax certificate for WA; include a clause that Redwood reserves the right to charge tax if material nexus is established in a jurisdiction where Harbor is not exempt. Request: procurement to provide a signed W-9 or local equivalent for our tax recordkeeping where applicable.

Next steps: I will upload OrderForm_Harbor_v4_tracked.pdf to the HubSpot link and circulate to Legal for a quick sign-off on clause wording. If Legal flags anything material I will call out the item. Planning to return to Samantha by Monday 18:00 PST.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Commercial Operations (Contracts)

Samantha —

Appreciate the timely redlines and the tax certificate. Neha and I reviewed the proposed tracked changes (attached) and we think the edits strike a fair balance. A few clarifications before we finalize the PDF:

- PO timing: to support consolidated tranche invoicing we need the PO number at least 5 business days before tranche billing date. Will Harbor be able to provide a PO per tranche as Neha requested? If helpful, we can accept a single master PO with tranche references.
- Proration mechanics: Language in the Order Form now states tranches do not roll forward; however, if Harbor requests carry-forward in writing within 30 days of tranche end we can evaluate case-by-case and apply a credit at Redwood's discretion.
- Tax paperwork: thanks for the certificate. For our Tax Ops we also need a signed tax form (W-9 for US entities) or local equivalent. I attached a short checklist in the tracked PDF for Harbor's finance team.

If those three items are OK, we'll upload the final OrderForm_Harbor_v4_signed-ready to DocuSign and send to your procurement contact for signature.

Next step for Harbor: confirm PO approach and attach signed W-9 (or confirm non-US tax docs). Once we have that, Redwood will prepare DocuSign package (Order Form + SOW if applicable) and set invoice cadence per tranche.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
